# Server configuration that produced these fixtures.
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.75 \
  --max-model-len 2048 \
  --dtype bfloat16 \
  --port 8000

# Environment required on this box (RTX 3060 Ti, 8GB, driver 595.71.05):
CUDA_HOME=<venv>/lib/python3.14/site-packages/nvidia/cu13
PATH=<venv>/bin:$CUDA_HOME/bin:$PATH
VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0

# Why VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0: flashinfer 0.6.14 bundles CCCL headers
# that fail to compile against the CUDA 13.3 toolkit shipped in the cu13
# wheels ("CUDA compiler and CUDA toolkit headers are incompatible").
# Only the sampling kernels are affected; attention and CUDA graph capture
# work. Falls back to the native PyTorch sampler. Does not change which
# metrics /metrics emits, but IS a deviation from a stock install and should
# be revisited on the H100.
#
# gpu-memory-utilization 0.75 (not 0.85): desktop/Chromium hold ~865 MiB, so
# 0.85 requested 6.5 GiB against 6.29 GiB free and failed at startup.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The `saturated` condition used a SECOND server config, identical except:
#   --max-num-seqs 4        (driven with 32 concurrent clients)
#
# Why: with the default batch size, 391,952 tokens of KV cache gave 191x max
# concurrency, so 16 concurrent requests never queued and
# num_requests_waiting stayed 0 across idle/single/burst. A fixture set where
# the queue-depth signal never leaves zero cannot validate the parser field
# that matters most. Capping the running batch at 4 forces the excess into
# the waiting queue: running=4, waiting=28, reason="capacity"=28.
#
# KNOWN GAP: vllm:kv_cache_usage_perc reads 0.00 in ALL four conditions --
# short prompts against a very large cache. That signal is untested by these
# fixtures and will need a fixture captured with long prompts, or on hardware
# where the cache is the binding constraint.
